newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler says July non-U.S. sales set record.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler says July non-U.S. sales set record.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said sales outside North America totaled 21,259 vehicles in July, a two percent gain over a year ago, and a record-setting month.
Sales for the month were fueled by rapid growth in South American markets, Chrysler said.
The previous sales record for any month was 21,177 vehicles, which was set in June, Chrysler said.
Non-U.S. vehicle sales in July 1996 totaled 20,750 units.
Non-U.S. sales from January through July were 137,435 vehicles, a nine percent increase from the January-July 1996 total of 126,223, the automaker said.
Total Latin America sales in July were 4,315, up 126 percent from a year ago. For the year to date, Latin America sales were up 138 percent from the 1996 January-July total.

Monthly Middle East/Africa region sales were 1,756, up two percent from July 1996. Sales in Europe were 9,749, off six percent from a year ago. Asia/Pacific sales totalled 5,439, down 19 percent from July 1996, Chrysler said.
